text: Try our cold coffee this weekend.
notes: The phrase is in the glossary as written.

text: Masala tea and a sandwich, ready in five minutes.
notes: Two entries, both as written.

text: Our menu now has a waffle and milkshake combo.
notes: Three single word entries.

text: Table booking opens at noon on Saturday.
notes: A two word entry.

text: Home delivery is free on every order above 500 rupees.
notes: Order here is a food order, the sense the glossary means.

text: New opening hours from Monday: 8 am to 10 pm.
notes: A two word entry.

text: Fresh cookies come out of the oven at four.
notes: Plural of a glossary word.

text: We baked three new cakes for the weekend.
notes: Past tense and plural.

text: Waffles and milkshakes are half price on Tuesday.
notes: Two plurals.

text: All sandwiches are made with bread we bake here.
notes: A plural ending in es, plus two exact words.

text: The chocolate cake is back on the menu.
notes: The longer phrase should win over cake on its own.

text: Our weekend offer: two coffees for the price of one.
notes: A phrase plus a plural.

text: Planning a birthday party? Ask about our discount.
notes: A phrase plus a single word.

text: Masala tea is our most loved order.
notes: The longer phrase should win over tea on its own.

text: Our chocolte cake sells out by noon.
notes: One letter missing inside a phrase.

text: Free home delivry on weekends.
notes: One letter missing inside a phrase.

text: Try the new milkshak flavours.
notes: Last letter missing.

text: Check our openning hours before you visit.
notes: One letter doubled.

text: Fresh biscuits with every tea.
notes: Biscuits means the glossary's cookie; nothing lexical can find that.

text: Food to go is packed in paper bags.
notes: To go means takeaway.

text: Grab a latte and a slice of cake.
notes: A latte is a coffee; cake is exact.

text: Save the date: our anniversary is on the 12th.
notes: A calendar date, not the fruit the glossary means.

text: We are rolling out new opening hours.
notes: Rolling out has nothing to do with a bread roll.

text: Our new seats are in mint condition.
notes: Mint condition, not the herb.
